name: Albury Wodonga Sailing Club
description: The Albury Wodonga Sailing Club sails on Lake Hume, about a 20 minute drive from Albury and Wodonga, and has been going since 1958. It is an Australian Sailing Accredited Discover Sailing Centre, running Discover Sailing Experiences, Tackers courses for 7 to 12 year olds, OutThere Sailing for 12 to 17 year olds, and dinghy, keelboat and powerboat courses. The club offers boat storage and boat registration for members, and each year hosts the Sail Country regatta on the weekend before the Melbourne Cup.
highlights: On the shores of Lake Hume, about 20 minutes from Albury and Wodonga
Australian Sailing Accredited Discover Sailing Centre
Tackers courses for ages 7 to 12 and OutThere Sailing for ages 12 to 17
Dinghy learn to sail, keelboat and powerboat courses
Sail Country regatta held the weekend before the Melbourne Cup
SailPass temporary membership and boat storage available

name: Border Bushwalking Club
description: Border Bushwalking Club calls itself Albury Wodonga's outdoor recreation club and has more than 100 members after 40 years of operation, with several foundation members still active. As well as bushwalking, the program covers canoeing, cycling, snow activities and volunteering. Members receive free entry to all club events, and the club is affiliated with Bushwalking Victoria, Rail Trails Australia and the Victorian High Country Huts Association.
highlights: Albury Wodonga's outdoor recreation club, running more than 40 years
More than 100 members
Bushwalking, canoeing, cycling and snow trips
Members receive free entry to all club events
Membership $50 a year, $45 concession, $90 family
Affiliated with Bushwalking Victoria and Rail Trails Australia

name: Murray Railway Modellers
description: Murray Railway Modellers is Albury Wodonga's model train club, with clubrooms at the Wodonga Showground off Wilson Street. Members meet every Wednesday night at 7pm and new members are always welcome. The club runs the annual Albury/Wodonga Model Train Show, held on 16 and 17 May 2026 at the Mirambeena Community Centre, with entry $10 adults, $5 children and $20 family.
highlights: Clubrooms at the Wodonga Showground off Wilson Street
Meets every Wednesday night at 7pm
New members always welcome
Runs the annual Albury/Wodonga Model Train Show
2026 show at the Mirambeena Community Centre, 16 and 17 May

name: Twin Cities Model Aero Club
description: The Twin Cities Model Aero Club has been the hub for model aircraft flying in the Albury-Wodonga region for more than 50 years. The field has a 130 metre concrete main runway with cross runways, an 80 metre concrete control line circle plus two grass circles, and dedicated areas for electric planes, helicopters, drones and free flight models. There is an air-conditioned clubhouse with kitchen, the field is open seven days a week and Sunday mornings are the busiest.
highlights: Flying field open seven days a week
130m concrete main runway plus cross runways
Control line circles and areas for helicopters, drones and free flight
Air-conditioned clubhouse with kitchen
Try n Fly introductory program
Busiest on Sunday mornings

name: Wodonga Men's Shed
description: The Wodonga Men's Shed is a place for men to come together, to socialise and to share or develop their skills and relate their experiences. Members take on wood and metal projects for private clients, community organisations and pre-schools. The shed also makes handcrafted wooden pens turned from Australian and exotic timbers, marsupial sculptures and firebox kits for camping.
highlights: Open Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings
Wood and metal work for community groups, pre-schools and private clients
Handcrafted wooden pens with engraving available
Marsupial sculptures and camping firebox kits
Men of any age welcome

name: Albury Men's Shed
description: Albury Men's Shed is a community workshop at Lavington where members take on woodwork, metalwork, craft and laser cutting projects. The workshop holds a range of machines and PPE including enclosed footwear is required in those areas. Visitors are welcome to come in and wander through the site, and service and support animals are permitted on lead in the non-workshop areas.
highlights: Open Monday, Tuesday and Friday mornings and Wednesdays until 2pm
Woodwork, metalwork, craft and laser cutting
Visitors welcome to walk through the site
PPE including enclosed footwear required in workshop areas
Member application form available to download

name: Albury & District Historical Society Inc
description: The Albury & District Historical Society works to collect, investigate, research, record, preserve, exhibit, discuss and publish material relevant to the region's heritage. It runs a program of meetings, research and publications and cooperates with the Albury LibraryMuseum. The society accepts research enquiries for an initial fee of $25 and publishes online photo galleries covering subjects such as the hundreds of homes demolished in Albury.
highlights: Collects and preserves Albury district heritage material
Program of meetings, research and publications
Research enquiries accepted for an initial $25 fee
Online photo galleries of historic Albury
Works with the Albury LibraryMuseum
Postal address PO Box 822, Albury NSW 2640

name: Wodonga & District Historical Society
addressLine: Hut 97, Bonegilla Migrant Experience, 132 Bonegilla Road
description: The Wodonga & District Historical Society collects and conserves items and information telling the story of the birth and growth of Wodonga and its surrounds. The collection is held in Hut 97 at the Bonegilla Migrant Experience on Bonegilla Road and is open Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 3pm. Research covers subjects including the railways, migration and the effect of the Second World War on the district, and monthly meetings are held at the Wodonga Football Club rooms in Vermont Street.
highlights: Collection housed in Hut 97 at the Bonegilla Migrant Experience
Open Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday, 10am to 3pm
Research on railways, migration and wartime Wodonga
Monthly meetings at the Wodonga Football Club rooms, Vermont Street

Visitors and prospective members welcome

name: Wodonga/Albury Camera Club Inc.
description: The Wodonga/Albury Camera Club is a group of keen photographers on the Victoria-New South Wales border who meet on the second Monday of each month at the Felltimber Community Centre in West Wodonga. Members work in both digital and film formats and the club runs competitions, workshops and outings. It is an incorporated body in Victoria operating under the Victorian Association of Photographic Societies.
highlights: Meets the second Monday of the month at Felltimber Community Centre
Competitions, workshops and photography outings
Members shoot both digital and film
Affiliated with the Victorian Association of Photographic Societies
Annual Paatsch Shield Challenge against Bendigo Camera Club

name: Albury Wodonga Amateur Radio Club
description: The Albury Wodonga Amateur Radio Club holds the callsign VK2EWC and draws members from both sides of the Murray River. Meetings are held at the 1st Lavington Scout Hall in Mutsch Street, Lavington, on the first Tuesday of each month except January, starting at 7.30pm. The club runs a Thursday night net at 8.30pm on 3.555 MHz and a Monday night net at 8pm on the VK2RAY 2m linked repeater system.
highlights: Club callsign VK2EWC
Meets the first Tuesday of the month (except January) at 7.30pm

name: Wodonga Urban Landcare Network
description: The Wodonga Urban Landcare Network has grown since 2012 to support member groups and hundreds of volunteers restoring waterways, hilltops and habitat around Wodonga. Its 18 member groups include Friends of Willow Park, Friends of Federation Hill, Friends of the Wodonga Rail Trail, the Multicultural Community Farm and Turtles Albury Wodonga. The network runs the Gardens for Wildlife and Healthy Hectares programs along with citizen science projects and community education events.
highlights: Network of 18 local Landcare and friends groups
Operating since 2012
Gardens for Wildlife backyard biodiversity program
Healthy Hectares program
Citizen science projects and community education events
Volunteer opportunities across all member groups

name: Albury Wodonga Theatre Company
description: Albury Wodonga Theatre Company is a not for profit run entirely by volunteers, promoting involvement in the performing arts in Albury-Wodonga since 1967. It stages two major musicals a year at the Albury Entertainment Centre or The Cube Wodonga, and up to three plays a year in its own intimate theatre space at 234 Olive Street, South Albury. The company also presents small ensemble, solo and cabaret style performances and takes proposals for new shows.
highlights: Volunteer run since 1967
Two major musicals a year at the Albury Entertainment Centre or The Cube
Up to three plays a year at its South Albury theatre
Cabaret, solo and small ensemble performances

name: Murray Concert Choir
addressLine: St David's Uniting Church, Wilson Street
description: Murray Concert Choir rehearses on Monday nights from 7.30pm to 9.30pm at St David's Uniting Church in Wilson Street, Albury. The choir began in 1982 under local teacher, musician and composer John Ross as the Murray Conservatorium Choir, and changed its name in 2022 when it became an independent community choir. It describes itself as a learning choir and welcomes singers who love to sing, with Catherine Nash as music director.
highlights: Rehearses Mondays 7.30pm to 9.30pm at St David's Uniting Church
Formed in 1982, independent community choir since 2022

name: Albury and Border Kennel Club
description: The Albury and Border Kennel Club is a not for profit, 100% volunteer run dog club that has been going since the 1930s, based at grounds in Eames Street off North Street. It runs a six week beginners obedience course using positive reinforcement, plus advanced obedience, agility, competition training and seminars. The club holds competitions in obedience, rally, agility, sprintdog and conformation, and spectators are welcome on competition weekends.
highlights: Volunteer run dog club operating since the 1930s
Six week beginners obedience course
Advanced obedience, agility and competition training
Competitions in obedience, rally, agility, sprintdog and conformation
Spectators welcome at competition weekends

name: Hockey Albury Wodonga
description: Hockey Albury Wodonga has been running hockey for Albury, Corowa, Rutherglen, Wangaratta, Wodonga and surrounding areas since 1953, playing out of the Albury Hockey Centre. It runs senior competitions, a twilight competition and masters hockey, plus Under 7s, Under 10s and Come & Try sessions for juniors. Representative teams play as the Spitfires and Junior Spitfires.

Based at the Albury Hockey Centre
Under 7s, Under 10s and Come & Try junior sessions

name: Albury Little Athletics Centre
description: Albury Little Athletics Centre has been running since 1990 at the Les O'Brien Athletics Precinct in East Albury, on a 400 metre synthetic track with wheelchair access. Track and field competition is on Saturdays from 8.30am and training is on Wednesdays from 5pm to 6pm. The 2026/27 season runs from 26 September 2026 to 27 March 2027, and multi-class events are offered alongside the standard age groups.
highlights: 400m synthetic track at the Les O'Brien Athletics Precinct
Saturday competition from 8.30am
Wednesday training from 5pm to 6pm

name: Albury Wodonga Football Association
description: The Albury Wodonga Football Association is the major organisational body for non-professional soccer across the Albury Wodonga region, north east Victoria and the southern Riverina. Twelve member clubs play under it, including Albury City, Albury Hotspurs, Albury United, Boomers FC, Melrose, St Pats, Twin City Wanderers, Wodonga Diamonds and Wodonga Heart. Alongside the senior Main Draw it runs MiniRoos junior football, women's, masters and all abilities competitions and a summer Twilight Football season, using grounds including Ian Barker Fields, Jelbart Park, Willow Park and Lavington Sports Ground.

Twelve member clubs
MiniRoos junior program
Women's, masters and all abilities competitions

name: Albury Basketball Association
addressLine: Lauren Jackson Sports Centre, 229 North Street East
description: Albury Basketball Association runs basketball out of the Lauren Jackson Sports Centre on North Street East in Albury. Seven affiliated clubs feed its junior domestic competition, including CC Celtics, Panthers Basketball Albury, PCYC Basketball Albury, SSA Basketball Club, Wildcats Albury, The Scots School Albury and Trinity Basketball Club. The association also runs senior domestic competition, Junior and Senior Cougars representative teams and basketball development sessions.

Junior and senior domestic competitions
Junior and Senior Cougars representative programs

name: Albury Grass Courts
description: Albury Grass Courts on Townsend Street in South Albury has been part of the region's tennis community for more than 115 years and plays on grass courts. The club runs coaching programs, social tennis, competitions and tournaments, and junior events including the Rex Hartwig Junior Cup. Courts can be booked online through play.tennis.com.au.

More than 115 years of operation

name: Wodonga Bridge Club
addressLine: Wodonga Senior Citizens Centre, 15 Havelock Street
description: Wodonga Bridge Club plays duplicate bridge at the Wodonga Senior Citizens Centre, 15 Havelock Street, Wodonga. Sessions are on Tuesday evenings, arriving 6.30pm for a 6.45pm start, and cost $4 for members and $6 for non-members including supper. Visitors are most welcome and a partner can be arranged on the day. The club also runs Learn and Play Saturday sessions through the year.

name: Albury Wodonga and Districts Car Club
description: The Albury Wodonga and Districts Car Club runs grassroots motorsport events on both sides of the border, including Lapdash rounds held at Wodonga TAFE and Motokhana and Khanacross rounds at Villa Grove. Events run as numbered rounds through the year, and memberships, event entries and club merchandise are all handled through the club website.

Motokhana and Khanacross rounds at Villa Grove
Multi-round motorsport calendar

name: Albury Wodonga Motorcycle Club
description: The Albury Wodonga Motorcycle Club is based on the Lincoln Causeway at Wodonga and is affiliated with Motorcycling Victoria. The club's listed disciplines are dirt track, motocross and speedway. Club contacts listed with Motorcycling Victoria are president Shane Clare and treasurer Kate Morey.
highlights: Track on the Lincoln Causeway, Wodonga
Dirt track, motocross and speedway

name: Albury Wodonga Motorcycle Enthusiasts Club
addressLine: Commercial Club Albury, Wattle Room, 618 Dean Street
description: The Albury Wodonga Motorcycle Enthusiasts Club is made up of riders who enjoy social get togethers, group rides and organised events through the year, and welcomes enthusiasts whatever they ride. It meets in the Wattle Room at the Commercial Club Albury, 618 Dean Street. The club provides conditional registration for NSW and Victorian motorcycles and restoration support, and runs regular Wednesday coffee runs, Sunday rides and the annual Butterball Rally.

Wednesday coffee runs and Sunday rides

name: Albury Wodonga Cycling Club
description: Albury Wodonga Cycling Club runs graded circuit racing on the outskirts of Albury on Saturday afternoons and criterium racing on Sunday mornings. The club covers road and track cycling, and many members also ride mountain bikes or compete in triathlons. Its calendar includes the Geoff Dixon Memorial, the John Woodman Memorial and the Ian (Woofa) Davis Memorial Cycling Festival, and it runs a Learn to Ride program.

Criterium racing on Sunday mornings

name: Albury Wodonga Equestrian Centre
description: The Albury Wodonga Equestrian Centre covers more than 97 hectares of purpose built equestrian grounds at the corner of Corrys Road and Roberts Road, Thurgoona, and reports more than 300 members. Facilities include an international cross country course, a main sand arena, a turf arena and polo X fields, the Roberts Road sand arena, a round yard, a stable complex with covered yards, and powered and unpowered camping. It hosts horse trials, showjumping, dressage, mounted games, polocrosse, clinics and training days for affiliate clubs and individual riders.

International cross country course

name: Albury Evening CWA Branch
description: The Albury Evening CWA Branch was created to fit in with modern day women's busy schedules and is aimed at professional women in Albury, Wodonga and surrounding areas. It meets every fourth Wednesday at the 2nd Scout Hall in Eames Street, North Albury. Members work on Country Women's Association projects, campaign on issues affecting country women and children and join interest groups, while keeping the traditional values of the CWA.

Meets every fourth Wednesday at the 2nd Scout Hall, Eames Street
Community projects and fundraising

name: Thurgoona Football & Netball Club
description: The Thurgoona Football & Netball Club, the Bulldogs, plays out of Thurgoona Oval on Table Top Road, known locally as The Kennel. It fields five male football teams from Under 12s to open age in the Tallangatta & District Football League, eight netball teams from Under 11s to open age in the Tallangatta & District Netball Association, and four female football teams in the AFL North East Border competition. The club is a not for profit set up to give the community sporting, social and recreation opportunities, with a strong focus on junior development.

name: Jindera Football Netball Club
description: Jindera Football Netball Club was established in 1899 and competes in the Hume Football Netball League. The club describes itself as community built, covering everything from Auskick to seniors, and fields seniors, seconds, Under 17 and Under 14 football sides alongside female football and netball teams. Memberships and club merchandise are sold through its website.

name: Albury Tigers
description: The Albury Tigers are Albury's football and netball club, established in 1876 and playing in the Ovens & Murray league. The club has grounds and rooms on Wodonga Place in central Albury which include a bar and function rooms. Memberships and club merchandise are sold through the club's online shop.

name: Wodonga Cricket Club
description: Wodonga Cricket Club was founded in 1869 and plays at Martin Park on Gordon Street, where it has two turf wicket ovals, Les Cheesley Oval and John Flower Oval, with electronic scoreboards, practice nets and clubrooms with a bar and kitchen. The club fields junior teams at Under 12, Under 14 and Under 16, senior sides in A Provincial, B Provincial and C Grade, and a women's team in the Cricket Albury Wodonga Thunder Stars league. It also runs an All Abilities program for ages 15 and over and Woolworths Cricket Blast for children from age 4.

name: Bungam Community Garden
addressLine: Corner Engelhardt Street and Stanley Street
description: Bungam Community Garden started in July 2015 on the corner of Engelhardt and Stanley Streets in Albury, where local residents from the surrounding neighbourhood adopt garden beds and grow produce in a shared space. It takes its name from its position near Bungambrawatha Creek, the area's largest waterway, and is easy to reach from the Bungambrawatha Creek Trail. Visitors are welcome to look around but are asked not to help themselves to produce grown by the volunteer gardeners.

name: Yackandandah Community Centre
description: The Yackandandah Community Centre is the town's neighbourhood house at 29 High Street, described as a space for the community to come together, learn from a range of courses, take part in activities and interest groups or browse the op shop. It runs the Yack Chat Cafe, a community garden and an op shop operated as a community social enterprise, and hires out rooms at $20 an hour along with equipment. The centre also runs a grants program for local initiatives and maintains a community directory.

name: Albury Horticultural Society
description: The Albury Horticultural Society has been operating for over 100 years and is a group of avid garden and plant lovers who may or may not have any formal qualifications. It meets on the first Thursday of the month at 7.30pm at the Albury Showground. The society is open to anyone interested in gardening and a little social outing.

name: Albury Chess Club
description: The Albury Chess Club was established in 1977 and plays every Friday night from 8pm until all games finish, at Albury High School in Kiewa Street. The club welcomes players of all standards, from novices and beginners through to the strongest players. It also runs competitions that bring schools and junior players together for titles and trophies.

name: Albury Wodonga parkrun
description: Albury Wodonga parkrun is a free, fun and friendly weekly 5km community event held every Saturday at 8am, starting from the Kremur Street Boat Ramp in West Albury. Participants can walk, jog, run, volunteer or spectate. The event is run entirely by volunteers, with weekly rosters and volunteer callouts posted through its Facebook page.

name: Hive Rotary Club Australia
description: Hive Rotary Club is a project driven Rotary club that meets fortnightly by Zoom and gathers in person in the Albury-Wodonga area every six weeks. Its projects include Paying It Forward, which takes students to community service projects, Hive & Honey, a social enterprise addressing period poverty through menstrual health and employment, and an environmental education project on Nusa Penida. The club also runs monthly fundraising barbecues and seasonal gift wrapping at Myer Centrepoint.
